Selects 1K blocks of 0000-1FFF: Y0 0000-03FF IC18, Y1 0400-07FF IC19, Y2 0800-0BFF IC20, Y3 0C00-0FFF IC21 (via LK1) or IC22 RAM (via LK2), Y4 1000-13FF IC23, Y5 1400-17FF IC24, Y6 1800-1BFF IC25, Y7 1C00-1FFF IC26. Enabled by MREQ (after link LK3) on G2A and A15 on G2B. G1 (pin 6) is not drawn in Fig. 6; it must be high for the decoder to work, assumed tied to +5V. Note: A13/A14 are not decoded, so this 8K block repeats at 2000,4000,6000 unless the Fig. 7 expansion is fitted.

'Link' in the MREQ line of Fig. 6 ('A link has been placed in the MREQ line so that the system may be expanded as shown in Fig. 7'). Tri-state octal buffer (81LS95 = 74LS465, both enables AND-ed, non-inverting) from internal memory bus MEM_D0..7 onto the system data bus. Pin 1 = RD, pin 19 = MREQ (after link) drawn; enabled only on memory read. Data channels are a fat arrow in the figure; bit n assigned to buffer n+1 (A1/Y1 = bit 0). Pinout verified against TI SDLS179. Kit sheet lists IC27 as 81LS97/98 - an 81LS97 (split enables) or 81LS98/96 (inverting) would NOT work here; use 81LS95/74LS465.

Address-bus bit to buffer-channel assignment for IC15/IC16 and data bit to channel assignment for IC27 are drawn only as fat arrows; assignments here are design choices (functionally equivalent), not read from the figure.

21L02 pins 1-10 and 14-16 (address, R/W, power) are not numbered in the figure; taken from the 2102/21L02 datasheet. R/W = WR_N is inferred from the WR line drawn to the RAM array with an arrow (no pin number printed).
2708 address pins and data pins 11/13/14/15 are not individually printed; from the 2708 datasheet and the drawn D7=17/D6=16/D1=10/D0=9 sequence.
